text:
[LREG.8.4] **An unsupported construct is a compile error, and the
diagnostic names the feature.** RE2 refuses backreferences (`\1`,
`\k<name>`), lookaround (`(?=`, `(?!`, `(?<=`, `(?<!`), possessive
quantifiers (`*+`, `++`, `?+`, `{n,m}+`) and atomic groups (`(?>`) on
its own, so this clause adds no rejection. It adds the two things RE2
cannot:

- the failure is at **compile time**, before a bundle exists; and
- the message is DS's own, naming the construct in the author's terms —
  "positive lookahead `(?=...)` is not supported by the RE2-class
  engine" — rather than surfacing RE2's parse error, `invalid perl
  operator: (?=`.

The code is `DS_VALIDATE_REGEX_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`.

**A compiler must not be stricter than RE2 either.** Refusing a pattern
RE2 accepts breaks [LREG.8.1] exactly as admitting a superset would,
because the set of patterns an author may write again differs from
RE2's. A scan that recognises unsupported constructs must therefore
model enough of RE2's grammar not to fire on their spellings elsewhere —
inside a character class, `[*+]` is two literal members, not a
possessive quantifier.

Authors needing these features model the value structure upstream (in
adapter parsing, a typed schema slot, etc.) rather than at rule time.
